post.caption: Damascene jewelry is gold hammered into steel. Damascene work inlays gold or silver wire into iron or steel. Its name alludes to Damascus, the Syrian city. First the steel is scored with a fine crosshatch pattern. Then the wire is hammered into the scored surface. Last, the steel is blackened in a hot bath, called pavonado. In Toledo, Spain, workshops still make it by hand. In 1761 King Charles III founded a royal arms factory in Toledo. The Zuloaga family revived the craft in Eibar in the 1860s. In January 2026 Toledo's damascene craft became a protected cultural asset.
